```{r cars,fig.width=10,fig.height=7}
library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)
setwd("~/Desktop/codes")

# ============ 1. Read data ============
da <- read_excel("~/Desktop/codes/data/Sp_Fig1_data.xlsx", sheet = "coverage")

# ============ 2. Re-bin ============
bin_levels <- c(
  "0",
  "0-1×",
  "1-10×",
  "10-100×",
  "100-1000×",
  "1000-10000×",
  "10000-100000×"
)

da <- da %>%
  mutate(
    cov_bin = case_when(
      coverage == 0        ~ "0",
      coverage <= 1        ~ "0-1×",
      coverage <= 10       ~ "1-10×",
      coverage <= 100      ~ "10-100×",
      coverage <= 1000     ~ "100-1000×",
      coverage <= 10000    ~ "1000-10000×",
      TRUE                 ~ "10000-100000×"
    ),
    cov_bin = factor(cov_bin, levels = bin_levels)
  )

# ============ 3. Count BGCs and percentages for each bin ============
bin_summary <- da %>%
  count(cov_bin, .drop = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    pct_raw = n / sum(n) * 100,
    pct_round = round(pct_raw, 2)  # keep two decimal places first
  )

# Adjust rounding error so the sum is exactly 100.00
diff <- 100 - sum(bin_summary$pct_round)
if (abs(diff) > 1e-9) {
  # Find the bin with the largest difference between raw and rounded values (most affected by rounding)
  idx <- which.max(abs(bin_summary$pct_raw - bin_summary$pct_round))
  bin_summary$pct_round[idx] <- bin_summary$pct_round[idx] + diff
}

print(bin_summary)

# ============ 4. Plot ============
bar_color <- "#7A3D9E"  

p <- ggplot(bin_summary, aes(x = cov_bin, y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = bar_color, color = "white",
           linewidth = 0.3, width = 0.85, alpha = 0.5) +
  # Add percentages above bars, rounded to two decimal places
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f%%", pct_round)),
            vjust = -0.5, size = 4.5, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(
    x = "Coverage of BGC (×)",
    y = "Number of BGCs"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 16) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x  = element_text(color = "black", face = "bold",
                                angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(color = "black", face = "bold"),
    axis.title   = element_text(color = "black", face = "bold")
  )

print(p)

# ============ 5. Export figure and summary table ============
ggsave("~/Desktop/codes/figures/Sp_Fig1.pdf", p,
       width = 10, height = 7, dpi = 600)
```
